subject: Clarify context-flooring and discount stacking for Acme Retail
messages:
From: Katie Jensen <katie.jensen@acmeretail.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Retail Procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: how do you aggregate & round tokens?

Diego — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked for one quick clarification so we can finalize the SOW: how exactly does Redwood handle token accounting for long-running chat sessions and streaming responses? A few specific asks below so we can reflect them in our purchasing model: 

1) When a single user conversation spans multiple requests (short prompts + many streaming responses), do you bill every call independently and round per-call, or do you aggregate across a conversational session? If aggregation: what window do you use (per minute/hour/day)?

2) Is there a minimum billing quantum for generation tokens and a different quantum for context (input) tokens? We want to reconcile this to our internal quota math.

3) How do committed discounts apply when a customer has a Dedicated pool + burst-to-hosted? Which usage is consumed against the committed bucket first?

We attached our draft SOW and a small sample of monthly usage patterns (usage_examples.csv). If you can reply with a short worked example we can drop into procurement. Appreciate it — Katie

--
Katie Jensen
VP, Product & Integrations
Acme Retail
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Katie Jensen <katie.jensen@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: how do you aggregate & round tokens?

Hi Katie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a worked example below. Attaching a one-page summary I can share with Procurement.

High-level: we bill in discrete metering "quanta" and have a conversation-level aggregation window used only for session-based SKUs (pilot/Dedicated). Public hosted usage is metered per-call.

1) Aggregation & windows
- Dedicated/pinned session SKU: we aggregate tokens at the conversation level across a rolling 24-hour window for the same session ID. That means small back-and-forths within 24 hours can be rolled together and billed against one bucket.
- Hosted (standard API) calls: billed per API call (each request/response pair), with per-call rounding to the quantum listed below.

2) Quanta (minimum billing blocks)
- Generation (model output) tokens: 12-token quantum per call (rounded up).
- Context/input tokens: 8-token quantum per call.
- Conversation-floor (session-level minimum): for Dedicated pilot SKUs we apply a 256-token daily floor per active session when aggregation is enabled; this is intended to stabilize unit economics for very chatty, low-traffic sessions.

3) Discount application (Dedicated vs Hosted)
- Committed Dedicated capacity consumes committed credits first (Committed pool -> Dedicated usage). Any Dedicated overage or Hosted API usage consumes against published pay-as-you-go rates.
- For customers with both Dedicated commits and Hosted overage, we apply committed discounts only to usage that runs on the Dedicated pool; Hosted requests are billed at the public API rate unless you purchase a Hosted volume discount add-on.

Worked example (simple)
- Customer A has a Dedicated commit for 5M tokens/month + 20% commit discount.
- A single user session in one day has: 180 input tokens across 6 requests and 1 streaming response totaling 620 output tokens.
  * Input billing: 180 rounded to 8-token quanta -> ceil(180/8)=23 quanta -> 23*8=184 billed input tokens.
  * Output billing: 620 rounded to 12-token quanta -> ceil(620/12)=52 quanta -> 52*12=624 billed output tokens.
  * Session total billed tokens (if on Dedicated session SKU with aggregation): max(256 session-floor, 184+624=808) -> billed 808 tokens (floor not triggered).
  * If the session only generated 120 billed tokens total, the session-floor would have resulted in 256 billed tokens for that day.

Notes: this conversation-floor only applies when aggregation is turned on (Dedication/pilot). For standard hosted API there is no session-floor — everything is per-call with the quanta above.

I'll loop in Ben for the discount stacking math and Marissa for SOW language if you'd like the 3-month onboarding credit as part of the SOW.

Attached: Acme_SOW_v1.pdf (draft SOW), one-page-metering-summary.pdf

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Katie Jensen <katie.jensen@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Jun 2028 10:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question: how do you aggregate & round tokens? (examples + discount stacking)

Diego / Marissa — quick calc and recommended language for procurement. Copying Katie for transparency.

Discount stacking rules (short):
- Committed discounts apply only to usage executed on the Dedicated pool tied to the commit.
- If the customer has a Dedicated commit and uses Hosted for bursts, that Hosted usage is billed at Hosted rates and does not draw down the committed bucket.
- We can offer a billing-side overlay credit (not automatic) to effectively extend commit pricing to Hosted bursts for a defined period; finance approval required.

Example math for Acme (numbers simplified)
- Committed: 5,000,000 tokens/month at 20% discount (Dedicated).
- Month usage: Dedicated-run = 4,200,000 tokens; Hosted-burst = 1,100,000 tokens.
  * Charges: Dedicated portion -> billed at committed rate: (5M list price * 0.8) prorated to 4.2M actual consumption -> charged on committed SKU.
  * Hosted portion -> billed at hosted list price for 1.1M tokens => no commit discount.
- If Acme requests commit-to-hosted bridging: for the pilot we recommend a negotiated overlay: apply the committed effective rate to up to 200k Hosted tokens/month for the first 3 months (credit memo), to give them predictable unit economics while they ramp.

Procurement language to propose (copy into SOW):
"Redwood will apply committed pricing to usage executed on the customer's Dedicated pool. Hosted API usage is billed separately at the public API rate. On a pilot basis Redwood will apply a billing credit up to 200,000 Hosted tokens per month for the first three (3) months to approximate committed pricing for burst traffic; this credit is a one-time concession and requires written approval from Redwood Finance"

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question: how do you aggregate & round tokens? (approval for pilot credit)

Thanks team — read the thread. Approved on the pilot concession as described. Approvals: 
- Grant a billing overlay credit that applies the committed effective rate to up to 200,000 Hosted tokens/month for 3 months (pilot).
- Waive the dedicated session 256-token floor for up to 100,000 total session tokens/month during the first 60 days of the pilot (this is narrow and limited to minimize economics risk).
